newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures closed mostly higher in slow trade on Wednesday on speculative buying by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,290 yuan ($397) per tonne, rising four yuan. It opened at 3,360 and hit a high of 3,380 yuan per tonne.
July fell 95 yuan to 3,200, November rose 30 to 3,378 and the January 1998 contract put on three to 3,385 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 9,200 tonnes from 15,000 tonnes.
Soybeans opened higher on speculative buying by retail investors and profit-taking pushed prices down, although closing levels were still higher than Tuesday's close.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading, but most investors remained sidelined on unclear market direction," one trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in a narrow range over the next few days.
